reason: This is a size word joined to a part (a short spur), and PO has no spur class to carry it. The bearers also differ (leaf base, sepal); like 'spurred' in the previous review, it should wait until a spur class exists.
The previous review mapped 'farinose' to PATO:0104364 mealy, so 'not farinose' is its negation.

label: cord-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being long, slender, cylindrical and tough but flexible, like a cord or rope.
reason: A real descriptor of roots and rhizomes (funiform) with no PATO or FLOPO term. 'Elongated' alone misses the cord-like build. It has few statements, so it should be checked before it is added.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: scalloped PATO_0001889 and dentated PATO_0001205)
reason: A hyphenated compound of two margin values for an in-between margin. It is handled by the pattern for a continuum between two values, like oblong-ovate.

It denies a callus (a hardened thickening), but no callus part or callose quality exists to negate. The sentences ('widened but not callous') also contrast it with another value, so on its own it says little.
Scrotiform means pouch-shaped (lips, sepal bases, hypanthia), which is what saccate is defined as.
Bladder-like fruits and calyces are inflated and air-filled; the examples themselves say 'bladderlike inflated'.
It means widely separated from the nearest parts of the same kind, which is the definition of distant.

target: new: compound of two co-occurring values of different attributes (scaly PATO_0001804 on the part; scales rust-coloured)
reason: It joins a covering (lepidote = scaly, as in the previous review) and the colour of the scales. These belong to two different bearers and qualities, so the word should be split rather than given a term.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer: base) + not tuberculate (FLOPO:0991060)
reason: It negates tuberculate only at the base of the fruit sides. A plain negation on the whole fruit would be wrong, and PO tubercle (an enlarged leaf base) is a different thing.
Ampullaceous means shaped like a flask (ampulla): swollen below and narrowed into a neck.

label: doubly toothed
definition: A dentated quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's margin bearing teeth that themselves bear smaller teeth.
reason: A standard botanical margin type with no term in PATO or FLOPO. Its natural parent is PATO:0001205 dentated (synonym toothed).
A spelling variant of 'inequilateral', which the previous review mapped to asymmetrical.
Serrate with blunt teeth. The adverb only describes the teeth's tip, and serrated is the safe nearest value.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: panicle-like FLOPO:0991198 and corymb-like PATO_0002455)
reason: A hyphenated compound of two existing inflorescence-form values, meaning a form between the two.
Partite means divided deeply into parts. PATO split covers this and is already the parent of pinnatipartite (FLOPO:0991156).

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: rhomboid PATO_0001938 and obovate PATO_0001936)
reason: A compound of two existing shape values, like oblong-ovate.
Half-nodding is a loosened 'nodding', which PATO drooping (bending or hanging downwards) covers. The 'semi-' qualifier goes into the approximate-value pattern, like the 'sub-' prefix.
'Storage roots' names a kind of root, not a quality. The nearest PO class is tuberous root, a root enlarged compared with the plant's other roots.
Virescent means green or turning green. The colour is PATO green.
'Sub-' plus ternate, meaning nearly divided into three. It is handled by the approximate-value pattern, like suborbicular.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (parallel to PATO_0002272; leaf rachis PO_0020055)
reason: A relation between a part and another named part, covered by the relational PATO quality 'parallel to'.
A many-headed (multicipital) caudex or rootstock is branched at the top into several crowns. 'Head' here is not a part class that could be counted.
Scales curling backward are recurved.
'Sub-' plus an existing shape value, so it is an approximate value, like suborbicular.
'Peristome anomalous' only says it departs from the usual type and does not say how. It is not a definable quality.

target: new: compound of two co-occurring values (papillose FLOPO:0991059 and reticulate FLOPO:0991100)
reason: The surface is papillose and reticulate at once, not something in between. Both values exist, so it is a conjunction, not a new term.

label: prorulate
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's cells projecting at their ends as small bumps where adjacent cells meet, so that the surface is roughened.
reason: A standard bryological term for moss leaf cells and setae. It differs from papillose (FLOPO:0991059), whose bumps arise on the cell surface, not at the cell ends.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (costa ending at or below the apex)
reason: 'Costa vanishing below / in the apex' gives where the costa ends compared with the apex. Its meaning (percurrent or not) depends on that other part, so the word alone cannot take a term.

target: docs/odp/03-count-of-parts.md (few to many flowers or leaflet pairs)
reason: A prefix cut off from 'pauci- à multiflores/multijuguées' (few- to many-flowered or -paired). The whole phrase is a count of parts, and the fragment alone is not a quality.
